US prosecutors have alleged that at least $4.5 billion was stolen from [USN:L6N45A0CE TEXT:"1Malaysia Development Berhad (1MDB)"], co-founded by former Malaysian Prime Minister Najib Razak, in a complex, globe-spanning scheme by high-level officials and their associates from 2009 to 2014. Malaysia has said billions more remain unaccounted for. In 2021, 1MDB [USN:L4N2MX1QM TEXT:"sued"] Deutsche and several other financial organisations to recover billions in assets that it said it were linked to misconduct related in the scandal. Deutsche said at the time that it was "not aware of any basis for a legitimate claim against Deutsche Bank." Lim Chee Wee, a lawyer for 1MDB, told a court in a separate case on Monday that the fund was in talks with Deutsche on a proposed settlement, The Edge financial newspaper reported, without providing details of the dispute. Lim said he had already passed on details about the talks to the Kuala Lumpur High Court, according to the report. Malaysia's court website showed that the court was scheduled to hear 1MDB's lawsuit against Deutsche and others on October 26. Lim declined to comment when contacted by Reuters. In an emailed statement, Deutsche said: "We continue to feel strongly about our position in the case, which is supported by our particular fact pattern that is differentiated from other defendants, as well as recent developments in ongoing similar cases involving other parties." "Any potential settlement would need to take this into account," it said.

item.title: Model blitz at Paris motor show as Europe-China rivalry heats up
item.description: Europe's car industry fought back against rising Chinese competition at the Paris car show on Monday with a wave of new model launches and fresh support from Brussels, even as Chinese automakers expanded their push into the region.
item.dc:creator: Nick Carey, Giulio Piovaccari
item.content:encoded: Europe's car industry fought back against rising Chinese competition at the Paris car show on Monday with a wave of new model launches and fresh support from Brussels, even as Chinese automakers expanded their push into the region. The show opened days after the European Union announced a deal with China to curb imports of Chinese hybrid vehicles into the bloc, with a [USN:B5N44302K TEXT:"cap"] of 350,000 a year, according to a European Commission official. While details of the arrangement have yet to be finalised, it was broadly welcomed by European manufacturers, though some said more support would be needed. Stellantis (STLAM.MI) CEO Antonio Filosa said the deal was a "good milestone", but that the Fiat maker was also seeking help with high energy costs from the Italian government and wanted Brussels to move more quickly on carbon emissions rules. The flood of Chinese hybrid imports into the EU is "not sustainable", Renault (RENA.PA) CEO Francois Provost said, describing the agreement as "better than a trade war". Zhao Fei, president of Chinese automaker Changan (000625.SZ) . said he was "not that concerned" by the deal, which he viewed as a precursor to "Made in Europe" local content rules that could be dealt with by setting up production in the region. Around [USN:L1N45S104 TEXT:"20 Chinese brands"], including BYD (002594.SZ) and Chery (9973.HK) , are attending the show, double their presence in 2024 as they seek growth overseas amid intense competition and weaker demand at home. Chinese brands have gained share rapidly in Europe over the last three years, while [USN:L4N45Y073 TEXT:"Chinese exports of hybrids"] to the EU's 27-member states tripled to $7.5 billion in the first half of this year, according to Chinese customs. The EU-China deal could hit BYD, Chery and state-owned SAIC's (600104.SS) MG brand hardest as between them they accounted for 90% of Chinese brand hybrid sales in the EU in the first eight months of 2026, Jefferies analysts said on Sunday. BYD said the deal amounted to short-term pressure but that it remained committed to Europe. Underscoring the challenges facing European manufacturers, Volkswagen said on Monday its deliveries fell [USN:L6N45Y0A9 TEXT:"14.3%"] in the third quarter, the steepest quarterly drop in four years, dragged down by a further decline in demand in its top market, China. Deliveries also fell in North America and Western Europe. As part of its efforts to regain market share in Europe, Stellantis is launching six new models across its European brands at the show and unveiling nine concept cars. On Sunday evening, CEO Filosa hailed "the reinvention of a European icon" as he unveiled an affordable retro electric version of [USN:L6N3SF0GW TEXT:"Citroen's 2CV"]. The company is also adopting faster Chinese-style development cycles, Chief Technology Officer Ned Curic said, outlining plans to build small EVs in Italy using a platform being developed with China's Leapmotor. Renault's head of growth, Fabrice Cambolive, [USN:S8N42Q0EZ TEXT:"said"] on Monday the carmaker could increase EV production in France by at least 50% over the next 12 months. 'IF THEY DROP EXPORTS ... THEY DIE' Like other Western motor shows, Paris had been in decline until Chinese automakers began turning up in force four years ago. Alongside BYD and Chery, this year's show features newer Chinese entrants including Aito, while state-owned Changan is launching its Nevo and Avatr brands in Europe. Chinese automakers also used the event to outline further European expansion plans. Changan's Zhao [USN:FWN45V1M3 TEXT:"said the company"] was in talks with manufacturers about producing vehicles in Europe and hoped to build its first European-made car in early 2027. BYD is [USN:L6N45Y0J7 TEXT:"studying the possibility"] of building a factory in France, Executive Vice President Stella Li told broadcaster BFM TV. The EU imposed tariffs on Chinese-made fully electric vehicles in October 2024. Brussels is also working on "Made in Europe" rules requiring minimum local content levels for EVs to access large parts of the bloc's market. Agreement between France and Germany on the provisions is "imminent", French President Emmanuel Macron said at the show. Chinese automakers have sought European production bases ahead of the proposed rules, often in partnership with established manufacturers. In July, China's [USN:L1N43P0D0 TEXT:"Geely Auto"] (0175.HK) said it would produce electric SUVs at a Ford Motor (F.N) factory in Spain. Separately, India's Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles and Stellantis [USN:L4N45Y0L2 TEXT:"said on Monday"] they had expanded their partnership to include technology and product development, with plans to build vehicles in India for more than 50 global markets. Car sales in China, the world's largest auto market, fell 20% in the first half of 2026, increasing pressure on manufacturers to expand overseas. As the US market is effectively closed to China's auto industry, Europe has become its top export priority. "If they drop exports in Europe they die because they can't make the money elsewhere," said Francois Roudier, secretary general of the International Organisation of Motor Vehicle Manufacturers.

item.title: Gold eases on strong dollar, oil prices; US inflation data eyed
item.description: Gold prices eased after touching a one-week high on Monday, pressured by a firmer dollar and higher oil prices, while investors awaited US inflation data for clues on the Federal Reserve's interest-rate trajectory.
item.dc:creator: Pablo Sinha
item.content:encoded: Gold prices eased after touching a one-week high on Monday, pressured by a firmer dollar and higher oil prices, while investors awaited US inflation data for clues on the Federal Reserve's interest-rate trajectory. Spot gold slipped 0.6% to $4,169.10 per ounce by 1:45 p.m. EDT (1745 GMT), having hit its highest level since October 2 earlier in the session. US gold futures for December delivery settled 0.6% lower at $4,190.60 per ounce. The US government and bond market are closed on Monday for Columbus Day. "We're seeing some selling pressure in gold because the dollar is near a one-and-a-half-year high," said Jim Wyckoff, a market analyst at American Gold Exchange. An escalating Middle East conflict kept investors wary. Investors would look out for remarks from Fed Chair Kevin Warsh, along with key inflation data, later this week to gauge future monetary policy. The US Consumer Price Index report is due on Wednesday, followed by the Producer Price Index and retail sales data on Thursday. "I don't think (the reports) are going to show any signs of easing in inflation, and they would probably lean bearish for the metals market," Wyckoff added. Markets largely see the Fed keeping interest rates on hold later this month, but assign 87.7% probability of a hike by December, according to CME's FedWatch tool. In a high-interest-rate environment, investors tend to favour yield-bearing assets over gold. Oil prices rose to near two-week highs on Monday as attacks on Saudi Arabia overshadowed possible further supplies to the market after US President Donald Trump hailed fresh Russian diesel exports and a Russia-Ukraine energy ceasefire. Among other metals, spot silver fell 1% to $60.22 per ounce, platinum eased 0.2% to $1,684.20 per ounce and palladium was down 0.5% at $1,141.90 per ounce.

item.title: Tencent eyes $4.5 billion bond sale amid AI funding push, source says
item.description: Tencent plans to raise at least $4.5 billion through a sale of US dollar and offshore yuan bonds, a person with direct knowledge of the matter said, as the Chinese technology giant ramps up spending on artificial intelligence.
item.dc:creator: Roshan Thomas, Yantoultra Ngui
item.content:encoded: Tencent (0700.HK) plans to raise at least $4.5 billion through a sale of US dollar and offshore yuan bonds, a person with direct knowledge of the matter said, as the Chinese technology giant ramps up spending on artificial intelligence. The sale is expected to be similar in size to Tencent's [USN:L1N42H00X TEXT:"$4.66 billion bond offering in June"], though the final amount has not been set and could change with market conditions and investor demand, the person said. The Shenzhen-headquartered company has also yet to finalise the size of each maturity tranche, said the person, who declined to be identified as the matter is private. Tencent did not respond to requests for comment on Monday. The potential deal follows a wave of technology company fundraising for AI. SoftBank [USN:L6N45F1AU TEXT:"raised $11.1 billion in bonds in September"] to fund its push into OpenAI, while Chinese AI developer Z.ai [USN:L1N455022 TEXT:"raised $5 billion"] through new shares and convertible bonds. But investors have become more selective about companies seeking to fund AI infrastructure buildout, with higher interest rates and bond yields affecting appetite. Nvidia-backed Australian AI data center operator Firmus this month [USN:L1N45U12T TEXT:"shelved a planned $5 billion initial public offering"] after drawing weak demand. CAPEX DOUBLED Tencent's capital expenditure more than doubled to 96.3 billion yuan ($14.4 billion) in the first half of 2026 from 45.9 billion yuan a year earlier, according to a stock exchange filing on Monday. The spending covered IT infrastructure, including computing equipment, software and data centres. Tencent said on Monday it proposes to issue notes under its global medium-term note programme and will provide potential investors with recent corporate and financial information related to the offering. The proposed offering comprises senior unsecured notes denominated in US dollars and offshore Chinese yuan, according to a term sheet reviewed by Reuters. Tencent may sell 10-year and 20-year US dollar bonds, as well as 10-year and 30-year offshore yuan bonds, subject to market conditions, according to the sheet. The company has not set a deal size. JPMorgan, Goldman Sachs, HSBC and Morgan Stanley are leading the dollar offering. ICBC (Asia), Agricultural Bank of China, Bank of China, Bank of Communications, China Construction Bank, CITIC Securities, HSBC and JPMorgan are leading the yuan tranche, the sheet showed. Banks are expected to arrange investor calls later in the day ahead of the potential offering, according to the sheet. Tencent said completion of the note issue depends on several factors, including market conditions, corporate funding needs and investor demand, and that no binding agreement has been entered into. ($1 = 6.6930 Chinese yuan)

item.title: Moonshot execs in talks to settle dispute with shareholder ahead of planned IPO, people say
item.description: While the dispute is not expected to jeopardise Moonshot's IPO plans, an unresolved fight with Recurrent could raise governance, ownership and disclosure issues for prospective investors.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Top executives of Chinese AI startup Moonshot are in talks ahead of its planned Hong Kong listing to settle a legal dispute with a shareholder demanding compensation for their alleged wrongdoing, people familiar with the matter said. Recurrent.ai, a developer of AI software, and some of its investors have accused Moonshot CEO Yang Zhilin and Chief Technology Officer Zhang Yutao of making false representations to Recurrent investors and enriching themselves at Recurrent's expense, according to a March 11 letter Recurrent's lawyers sent to Moonshot's investors, which was seen by Reuters. Yang and Zhang Yutao co-founded Recurrent.ai in 2016, before they established Moonshot in 2023, and continue to be directors of Recurrent's holding company, according to corporate records. The settlement talks have not been previously reported. Reuters could not independently determine the accuracy of the letter's claims. The letter did not name the Recurrent investors. Yang and Zhang Yutao did not respond to emailed requests for comment. Yang has previously denied the allegations. Moonshot declined to comment. David Morrison, senior partner at MinterEllison, which represents Yang, Zhang Yutao and Moonshot, told Chinese media in November 2024 the case "lacked both legal and factual basis" and that the law firm would mount a defence. Reuters could not ascertain if Zhang Yutao has commented publicly on the allegations. Recurrent did not respond to an emailed request for comment. Beijing-based Moonshot is among a group of Chinese AI developers, including DeepSeek, that is challenging the dominance of US companies such as OpenAI and Anthropic. Moonshot [USN:L1N44V07O TEXT:"confidentially filed"] for a Hong Kong IPO, Reuters reported in September, as it seeks to capitalise on the popularity of its Kimi AI models. While the dispute is not expected to jeopardise Moonshot's IPO plans, an unresolved fight with Recurrent could raise governance, ownership and disclosure issues for prospective investors, and complicate the listing process, said one of the people with knowledge of the dispute. The people familiar with the dispute said they did not know whether a settlement was imminent. The Hong Kong Stock Exchange and the Securities and Futures Commission, which regulates the city's financial industry, declined to comment. The China Securities Regulatory Commission and the Cyberspace Administration of China, one of the country's main AI regulators, did not respond to requests for comment. RECURRENT'S CASE AGAINST MOONSHOT EXECUTIVES The dispute, which is in arbitration in Hong Kong, has been going on since 2024. Recurrent has accused Yang and Zhang Yutao of setting up Moonshot without authorisation from the Recurrent board, making false representations to investors and enriching themselves at Recurrent's expense, according to the March letter from its lawyers. The letter alleged, without providing evidence, that servers containing vital large-language-model data were transferred without authorisation from Recurrent to a Moonshot subsidiary in April 2023, and that some other key data was deleted in September 2024 at Zhang Yutao's instructions. Recurrent and its investors are also considering a separate Cayman Islands legal action against Moonshot President Zhang Yutong, according to the letter. Zhang Yutong, who resigned as a Recurrent director in 2022, received a significant shareholding in Moonshot "for her personal benefit, a fact which was deliberately concealed from Recurrent's shareholders," it said. Reuters could not confirm this claim. Zhang Yutong also did not respond to several emailed requests for comment sent via Moonshot. Reuters could not ascertain if Zhang Yutong has commented publicly on the allegations. Chinese media, including state-backed online news publication The Paper, tech-focused LatePost and Tencent News, have reported that Yang, in a post in 2024 on his personal WeChat social media account, rejected the accusations of illegal enrichment and other wrongdoing, saying he had cut a deal with the Recurrent board members on setting up Moonshot and that Zhang Yutong's compensation was based on her professional capabilities. Reuters could not access the original post. Recurrent received 9.5% of Moonshot's original shares when the startup was established. Recurrent and its investors are seeking compensation equal to 10.5% of Moonshot's original shares, which could be worth more than $700 million based on Moonshot's $30 billion valuation in a June fundraising, one person said. Moonshot initially gained traction with its Kimi chatbot, known for processing long documents. Alibaba's (9988.HK) backing helped raise its profile, and the company has since expanded into coding, reasoning and agent-based AI products. In July Moonshot unveiled Kimi K3, a 2.8 trillion-parameter model that it said is the world's largest open-weight AI system and delivers performance approaching that of Anthropic's models. Its other backers include Tencent Holdings (0700.HK) , Meituan (3690.HK) and China Mobile (600941.SS) .

item.title: At least 72 Sudanese artisanal miners killed in strike, rights monitor says
item.description: At least 72 artisanal miners were killed in an airstrike in northern Sudan close to the Egyptian border, rights monitor Emergency Lawyers said on Sunday, in the second such incident in recent months.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: At least 72 artisanal miners were killed in an airstrike in northern Sudan close to the Egyptian border, rights monitor Emergency Lawyers said on Sunday, in the second such incident in recent months. Emergency Lawyers blamed the Egyptian air force for the strike, which it said took place on Saturday. In a statement on Monday, the Egyptian military said the latest phase of its campaign against illegal gold mining in southern Egypt was being carried out, after warning leaflets had been dropped on "criminal elements". The military made no reference to the airstrike in northern Sudan or the deaths of the miners. The campaign, launched in June, aimed to "impose the full authority of the state within Egyptian territory and protect its capabilities and national resources," the statement added. Egypt's foreign ministry did not immediately respond to a request for comment on the airstrike, but on Monday Foreign Minister Badr Abdelatty said on X that he had "reaffirmed" with his Sudanese counterpart "our historic fraternal ties and commitment to continued coordination and consultation." Sudan's army-led government said on Monday the incident occurred in a border area between Sudan and Egypt and that it was investigating. "It is important to treat this incident seriously, guaranteeing the uncovering of facts, and the protection and respect of borders." The Sudanese government said Sudanese and Egyptian leaders had been in contact immediately after the strike but it stopped short of directly blaming Egypt. Two Egyptian security officials said the strike was intended to end a state of "chaos" along the border and efforts by Egyptian and Sudanese groups to seize control of mining areas. Images shared on social media and by local rights groups, but not verified by Reuters, showed dozens of bodies strewn among rubble and others wrapped in funeral shrouds, and miners describing an airstrike on the area. Emergency Lawyers said such a cross-border attack would violate international law. Northern Sudan has seen an influx of artisanal miners and makeshift gold mining operations since the country's civil war upended traditional livelihoods. Gold has become a critical source of revenue for both sides in the conflict, and experts and industry participants say much of the metal is smuggled into neighbouring Egypt. Airstrikes in June targeted a group suspected of illegal gold mining, smuggling and drug trafficking, killing an unspecified number, Egyptian military officials said at that time, which they said occurred on Egyptian territory. The border between Egypt and Sudan is porous, and under dispute in two mineral-rich regions known as Halayeb and Shalateen. The war between Sudan's army and the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces has seen an increased frequency of mass-casualty events, particularly as drone warfare becomes the primary mode of fighting. On Friday, some 31 people were killed in a drone strike on a displacement camp in an army-controlled area of Sudan's Blue Nile state, one of the war's frontlines, according to the United Nations.

item.title: US Republicans, Democrats want Trump to reverse course on Russia diesel
item.description: Senator Thom Tillis said Trump's deal with Russia will put American lives at risk.
item.dc:creator: Jan Wolfe, Patricia Zengerle
item.content:encoded: Republican and Democratic US senators called on President Donald Trump on Sunday to "reverse course" on his [USN:S0N43U024 TEXT:"diesel supply deal"] with Russia , saying it runs counter to US law barring imports of energy until Russia ends its aggression against Ukraine. "Congress explicitly banned Russian energy imports in 2022 to prevent American dollars from financing (Russian President Vladimir) Putin’s brutal war against Ukraine," the seven senators - four of Trump's fellow Republicans and three Democrats - said in a statement. They also said that the administration failed to consult with Congress or submit any explanation of its decision, something also required by law. "The United States should not provide Putin with a financial lifeline while Russia continues to kill Ukrainian civilians. The Administration must immediately reverse course," the statement said. It was only the latest bipartisan criticism of Trump's deal, a shift from his party's near-unanimous support for Trump's foreign policy decision weeks before November 3 midterm elections that will determine whether his Republicans will retain their control of Congress. It was issued by Republican Senators Susan Collins of Maine, Lisa Murkowski of Alaska, Thom Tillis of North Carolina and John Curtis of Utah and Democrats Jeanne Shaheen of New Hampshire, Richard Blumenthal of Connecticut and Ron Wyden of Oregon. Tillis had said earlier on Sunday that the diesel deal may be illegal and would put American lives at risk. Trump said on Friday that Russia had agreed to supply diesel to global markets, and his administration temporarily lifted US sanctions on Russian fuel designed to deprive Moscow of revenue for its war on Ukraine . “I do believe there’s a legitimate case for saying the president’s not following the law,” Tillis, who is retiring from the Senate in January, told NBC's "Meet the Press." Prices for diesel — used for agriculture, heating homes and trucking — are near record highs and could hurt Republicans in next month's congressional elections . Analysts have said that Trump's agreement with Moscow was unlikely to lead to sustained lower fuel prices. ADMINISTRATION DEFENDS PACT US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent told Fox News on Sunday that the Trump administration will follow through with the deal using existing legal authority, and the agreement was good for the American people and would bring prices down. "We're going to do it with all the legal authorities we have. So, you know, anyone in Congress who says whether it's an old bill or the current Lindsey Graham bill (that) prohibits us from doing it is wrong," Bessent told "Fox & Friends." Trump last month signed a [USN:L1N4570ZO TEXT:"sweeping Russia sanctions bill"] into law, called the "Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026," to honor the South Carolina Republican and longtime Russia hawk who died in July. Some other Republicans had also criticized the diesel plan. Retiring Representative Don Bacon of Nebraska said on X on Friday that "propping up Putin's war economy is morally wrong as he uses that money to bomb cities." Mike Pence, Trump's former vice president, called his decision to lift sanctions on Russian oil a "betrayal" of Graham’s legacy and urged the president to "rescind" it. As Trump's poll numbers have [USN:L6N45D0NV TEXT:"cratered"], congressional Republicans have increasingly [USN:L4N45N1R0 TEXT:"distanced themselves"] from the president, on matters ranging from the conflict in Iran to the trade war with Canada . But the Senate's No. 2 Republican, John Barrasso of Wyoming, defended the diesel pact, telling CBS' "Face the Nation" that Trump is focused on bringing costs down. "The president is balancing and has to make tough decisions," Barrasso said. Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney in a call on Sunday with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy made it clear that the diesel deal "is in direct opposition to the efforts of Ukraine, Canada , and our allies to create peace and stability in Europe ," his office said in a statement. In a social media post on Sunday, Trump claimed that Ukraine and Russia had agreed to what he described as an "energy ceasefire" taking effect immediately, but did not elaborate. Zelenskiy said he was still waiting to see details of that agreement. "Ukraine supports the ceasefire, and it is important that Russia support it as well," Zelenskiy said on the Telegram app. There was no word from Moscow on the announcement, which followed days of US pressure on Ukraine to halt its attacks on Russian oil refineries.

item.title: OFRBS Summary
item.description: Wall Street ouvre en demi-teinte, prudence face au pétrole
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Wall Street ouvre en demi-teinte, prudence face au pétrole 12 octobre (Reuters) - La Bourse de New York a ouvert sur de faibles variations lundi, les investisseurs se montrant prudents face à la hausse des cours pétroliers, en attendant les résultats des grandes banques américaines à partir de demain. LVMH: Ventes inférieures aux prévisions au T3 avec le recul de la division mode et maroquinerie 12 octobre (Reuters) - Le groupe de luxe français LVMH a fait état lundi d'une croissance organique de ses ventes inférieure aux attentes des analystes au troisième trimestre, la demande pour ses marques de mode et de maroquinerie s'étant détériorée en raison de la faiblesse du marché en Chine. France-Des réfrigérateurs de centaines de supermarchés déréglés par une cyberattaque PARIS, 12 octobre (Reuters) - Les systèmes de réfrigération de plusieurs centaines de supermarchés Intermarché et U ont été piratés dans la nuit de dimanche à lundi en France, ont déclaré ces acteurs de la grande distribution, ajoutant que l'incident les avait contraints à jeter des aliments. BCE: Les anticipations d'inflation à court terme des ménages sont en hausse - Sleijpen FRANCFORT, 8 octobre (Reuters) - Les anticipations d'inflation à court terme des ménages dans la zone euro ont augmenté, même si celles à plus long terme restent bien ancrées autour de l'objectif de 2% fixé par la Banque centrale européenne (BCE), a déclaré jeudi Olaf Sleijpen, membre de l'institution de Francfort et gouverneur de la banque centrale néerlandaise. La BCE s'abstient de donner des indications sur les taux - compte-rendu FRANCFORT, 8 octobre (Reuters) - L'inflation dans la zone euro pourrait s'avérer plus élevée que prévu, mais la Banque centrale européenne (BCE) a jugé essentiel de ne de ne pas laisser entendre que de nouvelles hausses de taux étaient à prévoir, afin de garder toutes les options ouvertes, montre le compte-rendu de sa réunion de septembre, publié jeudi. BCE: Wunsch contre un relèvement du ratio de réserves obligatoires des banques FRANCFORT, 8 octobre (Reuters) - La projet de la Banque centrale européenne (BCE) visant à relever le ratio de réserves obligatoires imposé aux banques commerciales pourrait nuire à la crédibilité de ses futures opérations, voire empiéter sur la politique budgétaire des Etats, a déclaré jeudi Pierre Wunsch, membre du Conseil des gouverneurs de l'institution de Francfort et gouverneur de la Banque nationale de Belgique. La croissance mondiale devrait se maintenir autour de 3% grâce à l'IA - FMI BANGKOK, 12 octobre (Reuters) - Les investissements massifs dans les infrastructures d'intelligence artificielle (IA) soutiennent la croissance mondiale qui devrait se maintenir cette année à environ 3% malgré la crise énergétique, a déclaré lundi la directrice générale du Fonds monétaire international (FMI), Kristalina Georgieva. L'accord entre Pékin et l'UE limite les importations de véhicules hybrides chinois à 350.000 par an SHANGHAI/PÉKIN, 12 octobre (Reuters) - L'accord conclu entre la Chine et l'Union européenne (UE) visant à limiter les exportations de véhicules hybrides vers le bloc, porte un coup aux constructeurs chinois de voitures électriques. Volkswagen-Baisse de 14% de ses livraisons au T3, la Chine pèse 12 octobre (Reuters) - Volkswagen a annoncé lundi une baisse de 14,3% de ses livraisons mondiales au troisième trimestre, sous l'effet d'un nouveau recul de la demande sur le marché chinois. Les VE ont représenté environ 60% des ventes de la marque Renault en France au cours du week-end PARIS, 12 octobre (Reuters) - Les voitures électriques ont représenté environ 60% des ventes de Renault lors du week-end écoulé, a déclaré le directeur général de la marque, Fabrice Cambolive, ce qui constitue un nouveau record pour le groupe dans un contexte de hausse des prix des carburants.

item.title: OFRMO Summary

item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: L'Iran est derrière le projet d'attaque contre la base de Fairford, dit Londres LONDRES, 12 octobre (Reuters) - Les ministères des Affaires étrangères du Royaume-Uni, des Etats-Unis, du Canada, de la France ou encore de l'Allemagne ont condamné lundi "l'usage d'attaques violentes de la part de l'Iran", après que la base aérienne britannique de Fairford a été la cible fin septembre d'un projet d'attaque terroriste présumé. Perquisition au domicile de l'élue démocrate Ilhan Omar, cible de Donald Trump WASHINGTON, 12 octobre (Reuters) - Des agents du département de la Sécurité intérieure ont mené lundi avant l'aube une perquisition au domicile de la représentante démocrate du Minnesota Ilhan Omar, dans la région de Washington, dans le cadre d'une enquête fédérale visant l'élue d'origine somalienne, a annoncé le département de la Justice. Le pape Léon XIV hospitalisé mardi, ses engagements annulés jusqu'au 20/10 CITÉ DU VATICAN, 12 octobre (Reuters) - Le pape Léon XIV sera hospitalisé mardi matin en vue d'une intervention chirurgicale visant à retirer un petit nodule situé dans l'un de ses poumons, a indiqué lundi le service de presse du Vatican. L'Allemagne confrontée à une "guerre de l'ombre" plus menaçante que la Guerre froide-ministre de l'Intérieur BERLIN, 12 octobre (Reuters) - Le ministre allemand de l'Intérieur, Alexander Dobrindt, a estimé lundi que la "guerre de l'ombre" à laquelle l'Allemagne est confrontée était bien plus menaçante que la Guerre froide, affirmant que cette situation soulignait la nécessité de renforcer le BfV, l'agence de renseignement intérieur du pays. Nobel/Économie-Les Américains Robert E. Hall et Michael Woodford récompensés pour leurs travaux sur la stabilisation économique STOCKHOLM, 12 octobre (Reuters) - Le Prix de la Banque de Suède en sciences économiques, communément qualifié de "Nobel" de l'économie, a été attribué lundi aux universitaires américains Robert E. Hall et Michael Woodford pour leurs travaux sur les modèles économiques fondés sur les décisions individuelles, qui contribuent aujourd’hui à orienter les politiques de stabilisation des banques centrales et des gouvernements à travers le monde. L'aéroport de Ryad restera fermé cette semaine après deux attaques meurtrières DUBAI/RYAD 12 octobre (Reuters) - Les autorités saoudiennes ont prolongé lundi pour le reste de la semaine la fermeture de l'aéroport international de Ryad, capitale de l'Arabie saoudite, après que ce dernier a été la cible de deux attaques meurtrières dont une samedi, revendiquée par les Houthis qui a fait 13 morts et plus de 300 blessés. Deux Palestiniens tués par des frappes israéliennes - secours LE CAIRE, 12 octobre (Reuters) - Des frappes israéliennes ont tué au moins deux Palestiniens dans la bande de Gaza lundi, selon les autorités sanitaires locales. Ukraine-Trump annonce un cessez-le-feu dans l'énergie, Zelensky attend des précisions Le président américain Donald Trump a annoncé dimanche la conclusion d'un accord de cessez-le-feu entre l'Ukraine et la Russie portant sur les infrastructures énergétiques et son entrée en vigueur, avant d'être rapidement contredit par son homologue ukrainien Volodimir Zelensky. La ministre allemande du Travail démissionne après le décès de sa belle-fille BERLIN, 12 octobre (Reuters) - Bärbel Bas, ministre allemande du Travail et coprésidente du Parti social-démocrate (SPD, centre gauche), a démissionné lundi de ces deux fonctions, invoquant le décès de sa belle-fille et les attaques politiques de plus en plus virulentes dont elle a fait l'objet. L'Arabie saoudite annonce des blessés dans une nouvelle attaque contre l'aéroport de Ryad Les autorités saoudiennes ont fait état de blessés lors d'une nouvelle attaque contre l'aéroport international de Ryad survenue dimanche, au lendemain d'un assaut contre ce même aéroport, revendiqué par les Houthis, qui a fait 13 morts.
